title: The First Spring

beats.t: There was no floor beneath the gap. The tiger fell, hanging from a single red thread. Someone above refused to let go.
I told you to let go. Just as stubborn as back then.
The sound of rain flowed down the thread. Not downward with the chain's pull, but sideways, where the thread led. The tiger changed course.
Not that way. Come down.
I'd like to, but the thread won't listen.
The thread blazed. The world blurred like wet glass. Beyond it stood an old bus stop. This time it wasn't a picture in a ledger. It had a smell.
Spring rain fell. Beneath the bus-stop roof sat two young women, not long out of their school uniforms.
Halfie, look. A weird app installed itself. It says customer support is the universe.
The universe does consultations too? How many stars?
Haven't rated it yet. I'll rate it when it replies. If it doesn't, one star.
The tiger looked down on the scene. The young woman on the left wore wet sneakers. It was her. Seo Hanbi at twenty-two, with a human face.
Halfie. Yes. That's what she called me. Because she shared half her umbrella.
The envelope's nearly full. We can really go to the sea next month.
Mine too! Let's count it together tomorrow, half each. Here, same time.
Yeoni held out a little finger. Seo Hanbi hooked hers around it. Their fingers were cold. Both laughed.
Tomorrow. That tomorrow never came.
The scene changed. A cramped studio apartment at midnight. Only the phone screen on the desk was lit. Yeoni slept beneath a blanket.
A notification appeared. Then another. The same sentence stacked up dozens of times: Vessel located.
I've never seen this scene before.
The thread wasn't showing only the tiger's memories. It was drawing in memories from its other end—Yeoni's—as well.
A black hand crawled out of the screen. One, two, three. They covered sleeping Yeoni's face. Yeoni couldn't even scream.
Ah, delicious. A full vessel at last.
Stop. Wake her up. Wake her!
The tiger's voice never reached that room. It was a spring already past. When the black hands withdrew, Yeoni opened their eyes. A round shadow floated behind them.
This face will do.
In the mirror, the corners of Yeoni's mouth rose. Once. Twice. The smile grew too broad, then the lips lowered again. Only on the third attempt did it resemble Yeoni's usual expression.
It wasn't her. The one that day was never her.
The following day. The same bus stop, the same time. Seo Hanbi arrived first, clutching a thick envelope. Rain had slightly blurred the words on it: Go to the sea together.
You're here? Where's your umbrella? Today I'll share my half.
Seo Hanbi.
Seo Hanbi stopped smiling. Yeoni had never called her that way. Her full name, surname included, in a businesslike voice.
Why are you calling me that? Is something wrong?
Give me the envelope. I'll count it.
Seo Hanbi hesitated, but held it out. Of course she would give it if Yeoni asked. Half each.
The moment Yeoni took the envelope, they turned away. They walked into the rain without an umbrella and never looked back.
Yeon? Yeon! Where are you going? We said we'd count it together tomorrow.
Why didn't you run after her? Why did you just stand there, you fool?
Seo Hanbi didn't follow. Her legs wouldn't move. Two buses passed. As the third arrived, someone ran into the bus stop.
A young man. He carried a white umbrella, still folded. He seemed to have run there without even taking time to open it. Water dripped from his hair.
His face was invisible, as though the thread had deliberately blurred that part. Only his voice was clear.
Man: Have you seen Yeoni? About this tall, yellow bag. I haven't been able to reach them since last night.
I did. Just now. She left with my money.
The white umbrella fell from the man's hand. He looked around through the rain. There was no one left.
Man: Too late. Again.
That voice. The cat's voice.
The man ran off again without retrieving his umbrella. Seo Hanbi stared at the white umbrella for a long time. She didn't pick it up. Other people's things were debts.
He was in that spring too. Arriving too late, he must have cried even longer than I did.
After that, Yeoni never returned. No calls, no texts. Seo Hanbi went to that bus stop every day, whether it rained or not.
On the tenth night, her phone lit up by itself. The same app that had appeared on Yeoni's phone. In place of the customer-support icon was a black circle.
After Yeoni vanished, one man remained at the bus stop. Park Byeongha. He would wear mismatched socks every day and watch the road where Yeoni never came.
Every time he asked Destiny Customer Support to open its closed door, he was refused. At last, the universe asked what he would pay to go back once.
Park Byeongha offered his human body and name. Spring returned to its beginning, and he opened his eyes as a white cat who didn't yet even have the name Yeoni would give him.
As that door closed, Seo Hanbi crossed with him, hanging from her chain. Not the one who began the rewind, but a witness to the failed timeline.
Do you feel wronged?
Who are you?
The child who abandoned you has become a monster. One that grows by eating other people's fortune. She will make gentle souls like you cry again.
Her? That can't be.
Who walked away with your envelope?
Seo Hanbi couldn't answer. Her nails dug into her palm. The tiger watched that hand from above. Her right hand.
I will give you a chance. Before she becomes a monster, collect what she has. Fortune, breath, applause.
Not for free, I assume.
Nothing is free. Surely you know that now.
Those words hurt most. Seo Hanbi laughed for a long time. It sounded like crying.
Fine. But give me a ledger. So no one can ever take from me for free again.
A golden ring fell from the screen and wound around her right wrist. Black fur covered her skin. Her fingers became claws. A soaked ledger dropped at her feet.
Stop. Don't take it. You mustn't take it.
The Seo Hanbi of the past didn't hear. A black tiger stood. Golden eyes opened for the first time. In them, too, were tiny black dots.
The thread jerked to a halt. The rain stopped. The tiger hung once more in the gap beneath the eclipse: the neck chain pulling down, the red thread up. Its body felt as though it would tear in two.
Have you seen? And what does that change?
Everything. She never abandoned me. You ate her. You took my envelope wearing her face.
And you became my hand. You put on the ring yourself. You opened the ledger yourself.
The tiger couldn't argue. It was true. She had been deceived. But her claws had collected the drummer child's applause. The voices of Expression. The hours of Wealth.
Yes. That was my hand.
Then remain my hand until the end. Where could you turn now?
The chain gave one great tug. The ring strangled her. Her golden eyes dimmed. Then a voice came down the thread from above.
Tiger! No, Seo Hanbi! Answer if you can hear me! I haven't asked my questions yet!
It wasn't Halfie. Still, the tiger smiled. The Yeoni of this spring was calling her properly by name.
Where can I turn? There is somewhere. Up there, to the girl holding the umbrella.
The tiger lifted its forepaw. The right one, where the ring had first closed. Extending its claws, it grasped the golden ring around its neck.
Break that ring and you become nothing. No body, no power, no road home.
I know. You said nothing was free. This time, I'll pay.
